title: Microcost Attribution Pivot & Export Flow — Pricing Pattern Kit
creator: Ariana Cho
description:
Goal: Design a compact pivot-style UI for token-level cost attribution that lets customers slice by route/model/session/organization and export large datasets safely. Deliver a small pattern kit showing how pricing tiers and per-token breakdowns are surfaced in the Console, plus a working Figma prototype for usability testing.

Scope:
- Pivot table-style interactions: drag-to-group, multi-column aggregations (sum tokens, avg latency, cost), and quick filter presets.
- Export flow: streaming/chunked CSV and Parquet export with progress UI, sampling preview, and optional anonymization of PII (user_id hashing).
- Pricing pattern recommendations: slab vs. continuous per-token pricing visualizations, rate-normalizer preview for customers on mixed model fleets.
- Performance constraints: ensure UI stays responsive for >100k rows by using server-side aggregation and incremental client render.
- Accessibility & localization: keyboard-first pivot controls, aria labels on column operations, i18n-ready labels.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype demonstrates drag-group across 3 dimensions and column pivoting in Figma.
2) Export modal includes format selection (CSV, Parquet), date range, sampling toggle, and a progress bar with cancel.
3) Pricing pattern tile shows both slab preview (discrete bands) and continuous curve with toggle; unit cost breakdown shows effect of batching and quantization recommendations (informational only).
4) Handoff assets (tokens: column schema) for ENG and Data team, and a short usability script for two 15-min tests.
5) Security checklist: export uses presigned S3 URL pattern (mocked in prototype) and anonymization option is present for PII-sensitive exports.

Notes on scope boundaries: This ticket is purely design + prototype. Backend export implementation, presigned URL generation, and RBAC enforcement are covered in ENG-48210 and PM-1149 and are dependencies for full rollout.
design_decisions: Use pivot metaphor instead of spreadsheet to keep interactions lightweight and avoid feature bloat.
Expose pricing pattern as a small card with two compact views (slab bands + continuous curve) to avoid cluttering core attribution flows.
Export modal defaults to sampled CSV for very large ranges and shows estimated file size before starting.
Anonymization is opt-in; default is to include route/session metadata but hash user IDs for compliance-conscious customers.
Client renders first N rows and streams the remainder to avoid blocking main thread; show progressive counts in UI.
Keyboard-first pivot operations, with an optional bottom-sheet cheat-sheet for power users.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Full spreadsheet parity would increase scope and maintenance costs; we deliberately scope to pivot-first patterns.
Large exports may create backend load; recommend rate-limited presigned upload flow and chunked generation on worker fleet.
Displaying raw user identifiers by default increases compliance risk; chosen default steers to hashed identifiers to reduce friction for SOC teams.
Complex pivot interactions might require additional microcopy and onboarding — we include short inline help and a 2-step guided tour in prototype.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype supports grouping by at least 3 fields and column aggregation toggles.
Export modal mock shows format, sampling, anonymization, progress, estimated size, and cancel behavior.
Design tokens and spacing variables added to Console token library for new pattern (ready for FE dev handoff).
Usability tests (n=6) show >80% success on two core tasks: create a 2-dimension pivot and export as CSV with anonymization enabled.
